'''Leo Reino Sario''' (18 May 1916 – 15 August 2009) was a Finnish-born mathematician who worked on [[complex analysis]] and [[Riemann surfaces]].

==Early life and education==
After service as a Finnish artillery officer in the [[Winter War]] and World War II, he received his PhD in 1948 under [[Rolf Nevanlinna]] at the [[University of Helsinki]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=13233}}</ref>

==Career==
Nevanlinna and Sario were founding members of the [[Academy of Finland]], and there is a statue on the academy grounds named after Sario.<ref name=oit>{{cite book|title=Otavan Iso tietosanakirja (Otavan Great Encyclopedia)|publisher=[[Otava (publisher)|Otava]]|year=1966|volume=7|page=1078}}</ref><ref name=sarioucla/> Sario moved to the United States in 1950 and obtained temporary positions at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]],<ref name="sarioias">[http://www.ias.edu/people/cos/users/5643 Sario, Leo Reino – Institute for Advanced Study Visiting Scholar]</ref> [[MIT]], [[Stanford University]], and [[Harvard University]]. In 1954 he became a professor at [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]], remaining there until his retirement in 1986.

He was the author or co-author of five major books on complex analysis and over 130 papers. He supervised 36 doctoral students, including Kōtarō Oikawa and [[Burton Rodin]].<ref name=sarioucla/>

==Awards and honors==
In 1957 he was awarded the Cross of the Commander of Finland's Order of Knighthood.<ref name=sarioias/> He was a [[Guggenheim Fellowship|Guggenheim Fellow]] for the academic year 1957–1958.<ref>{{cite web|title=Leo Sario|website=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/leo-sario/}}</ref>

Ahlfors and Leo Sario|journal=[[Canadian Mathematical Bulletin]]|volume=4|issue=2|year=1961|pages=195–196|url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/3C05A49C816789547FB08EEB623C6BF3/S0008439500025777a.pdf/-riemann-surfaces-by-lars-v-ahlfors-and-leo-sario-princeton-mathematics-series-26-princeton-university-press-1960-xi-382-pages.pdf|doi=10.1017/S0008439500025777|doi-access=free}}</ref> [https://books.google.com/books?id=qgTWCgAAQBAJ 2015 pbk reprint]
*with Kiyoshi Noshiro: Value Distribution Theory, Van Nostrand 1966<ref name="Jenkins1969">{{cite journal|last1=Jenkins|first1=James A.|author-link=James Allister Jenkins|title=Book Review: ''Value distribution theory''|journal=Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society|volume=75|issue=5|year=1969|pages=917–924|issn=0002-9904|doi=10.1090/S0002-9904-1969-12286-X|doi-access=free}}</ref> [https://books.google.com/books?id=TMrkBwAAQBAJ 2013 pbk reprint]
*with Burton Rodin: Principal Functions, Springer 1968, Van Nostrand 1968; [https://books.google.com/books?id=_ZnlBwAAQBAJ 2012 pbk reprint]
*with Kōtarō Oikawa: Capacity Functions, Grundlehren der mathematischen Wissenschaften 149, Springer 1969
*with Mitsuru Nakai: Classification Theory of Riemann Surfaces, Grundlehren der mathematischen Wissenschaften 164, Springer 1970; [https://books.google.com/books?id=I7_sCAAAQBAJ 2012 pbk reprint] 
*with Mitsuru Nakai, Cecilia Wang, Lung Ock Chung: Classification Theory of Riemannian Manifolds : Harmonic, quasiharmonic and biharmonic functions, Lecture Notes in Mathematics 605, Springer 1977; [https://books.google.com/books?id=YVx7CwAAQBAJ 2006 pbk reprint]
